title: WHAT COULD MY SUBSCRIPTION BUSINESS LOOK LIKE?
content:
If you want to own a subscription, the next question is what continuing value the customer would pay to keep receiving or accessing.

Four common directions are software or tools, ongoing content, membership/community, and ongoing support or coaching. These can overlap, but it helps to identify what the customer is fundamentally paying for.

SOFTWARE OR TOOL
The customer pays for continued use of functionality. The business must maintain enough usefulness and reliability to justify continued payment.

CONTENT SUBSCRIPTION
The customer pays for continued access to or delivery of useful content. The ongoing production burden and the reason customers stay both matter.

MEMBERSHIP OR COMMUNITY
The customer pays for continued membership, access, resources, connection, or a combination. A community needs a reason to exist beyond simply putting people in the same online space.

ONGOING SUPPORT OR COACHING
The customer pays for continued access to help, guidance, accountability, implementation support, or expertise. This can create recurring revenue while remaining heavily dependent on your time unless delivery is designed carefully.

CHOOSE BY THE VALUE, NOT THE BILLING INTERVAL
Do not start with "I want $29 per month." Start with what a customer would continue receiving and why stopping payment would reasonably end that value.

SOFTWARE / TOOL → PDF 33.
CONTENT → PDF 34.
MEMBERSHIP / COMMUNITY → PDF 35.

ONE OFFER CAN CONTAIN MORE THAN ONE ELEMENT

A software subscription might include a member community. A membership might include monthly content. Coaching might include a resource library. The branch should follow the primary reason the customer keeps paying.

If the software disappeared and the offer would no longer make sense, software is probably primary. If the real value is access to you, support/coaching may be primary even if customers also receive content.
